title: The Big Show
paragraphs: NBC celebrity variety revue hosted by Tallulah Bankhead. The frozen GRH set preserves 30 dated broadcasts/edited rebroadcasts from 1950-52; it is a partial preservation set rather than a complete run. Exact same-date RadioGOLDINdex records are matched by date and closest surviving duration.

GRH documents the program through Preserved first-season span (November 5, 1950 to May 6, 1951) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] and Preserved later-season span (September 30, 1951 to March 9, 1952) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Tallulah Bankhead (host on 30 recordings and performer on 29 recordings), Meredith Willson (music director on 29 recordings), Meredith Willson and His Orchestra (performer on 29 recordings), Dee Englebach (director on 27 recordings and producer on 27 recordings), Goodman Ace (performer on 11 recordings and writer on 11 recordings), Morton Green (writer on 22 recordings), and Ed Herlihy (announcer on 20 recordings).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include celebrity variety and revue, comedy and comic performance, popular music and orchestral performance, and Hollywood and Broadway celebrity culture.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including NBC prestige variety radio, Tallulah Bankhead as radio variety host, Network radio during television expansion, and Full-network and condensed rebroadcast preservation.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]] (44 shared credited people), [[show|the-fred-allen-show|The Fred Allen Show]] (20 shared credited people), [[show|duffys-tavern|Duffy's Tavern]] (22 shared credited people), [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]] (21 shared credited people), and [[show|fibber-mcgee-and-molly|Fibber McGee and Molly]] (12 shared credited people).
